items.question: Why do some beings attain a level even higher than that enjoyed by Īśa?
premises: A trace of impurity causes a state of higher-and-lower differentiation.
The level enjoyed by Īśa is still marked by that differentiated condition.
Some beings can share in a level above that Īśa-enjoyed state.
items.inference: Because impurity still qualifies the Īśa-level, beings who transcend that qualification can attain a higher level.
uncertainties: The exact referent of ūrdhvapadabhāginaḥ (which class of beings) is not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Because a slight stain of impurity produces a state of higher and lower, even the level enjoyed by Īśa remains within that differentiation; therefore some beings can partake of a level higher than that.

items.question: What arises from eagerness to manifest māyā in one bearing its impressions?
premises: There is an eagerness to manifest māyā.
A subject may be imbued with the impressions of that māyā.
From this condition arises deliberation marked by many activities and variety.
items.inference: Eagerness to manifest māyā in one bearing its impressions gives rise to varied, activity-filled deliberation.
uncertainties: The precise agent of vividhamantraṇam is implied rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: From eagerness to manifest māyā, in one who bears its impressions, there arises a varied deliberation consisting in the undertaking of many activities.

items.question: What is the nature of the state that appears from the stream of great knowledge?
premises: Something bestowing Śiva has appeared from the stream of great knowledge.
In that context a lower state is present.
That lower state is closed off by the supreme state.
items.inference: The manifestation from great knowledge bestows Śiva, yet it includes a lower state that remains veiled by the supreme state.
uncertainties: Whether prādurbhūtaṃ refers to the same entity as bhāvaḥ or to a prior manifestation is slightly compressed in the verse.
items.plain_english: What has appeared from the stream of great knowledge bestows Śiva; indeed, in that context the lower state is closed off by the supreme state.

items.question: Why do followers of Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, and other teachings fail to reach firm establishment?
premises: Firm establishment is not attained in the impure higher domain.
Followers of Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, and other teachings remain established within those teachings.
Their position is comparable to remaining in that impure higher domain.
items.inference: Because they remain within teachings aligned with the impure higher domain, they do not attain firm establishment.
uncertainties: The exact scope of śāsanāntara is open, though the verse gives Vaiṣṇava and Buddhist as examples.
items.plain_english: It would not attain firm establishment, as in the impure higher domain; therefore those established in Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, and other teachings do not reach that firm establishment.

items.question: How do those refined by Śaiva teaching differ from others in attaining complete liberation?
premises: Some are not completely liberated.
Those refined by Śaiva teaching are not in that same condition.
This applies across atimārga, krama, kula, trika, and other streams.
items.inference: Those refined by Śaiva teaching, across its various streams, are not left incompletely liberated in the way others are.
uncertainties: The verse states a contrast but does not specify the exact mechanism of their liberation.
items.plain_english: Just as some are not completely liberated, those refined by Śaiva teaching are not so, whether in the atimārga, krama, kula, trika, or other streams.

items.question: Is there any difference in attaining liberation among those properly initiated in the Parameśāna scripture?
premises: Some people are properly initiated in the Parameśāna scripture.
Liberation is something that can be attained.
The verse denies any difference among them in that attainment.
items.inference: For those properly initiated in the Parameśāna scripture, there is no difference whatsoever in attaining liberation.
items.plain_english: But for those people who are properly initiated in the scripture of Parameśāna, there is no difference whatsoever in the attainment of liberation.

items.question: Is there any means to liberation other than the one taught here?
premises: A means to liberation has been indicated.
No other means to liberation exists apart from it.
In some cases the result comes effortlessly and through the sequence of living liberation.
items.inference: There is no alternative means to liberation, though its realization may vary in ease and in following the path of living liberation.
uncertainties: The antecedent of etad is not explicit in this verse and depends on the immediate context.
items.plain_english: There is no means to liberation whatsoever other than this; only, in some cases, it comes effortlessly and through the sequence of liberation while still living.

items.question: How quickly is supreme attainment reached in these teachings compared with other methods?
premises: Supreme attainment can arise quickly in our teachings.
In some cases attainment follows the methodical sequence of tattva-series yoga.
That methodical sequence may take a long time.
items.inference: Our teachings can yield supreme attainment quickly, whereas some tattva-series methods yield it only after a long time.
uncertainties: The contrast is compressed; the verse implies but does not fully spell out the opposing system.
items.plain_english: In our teachings supreme attainment comes quickly indeed; in some cases, by contrast, it comes only after a long time through the methodical sequence of yoga based on the series of tattvas.

rows.grounds: adverb of consequence; sandhi form of tataḥ

items.question: Why is it fitting to describe manifestation as shining forth in the form of emanation?
premises: The waking state and the other states each have manifold divisions.
Those divisions will be determined later.
Given that multiplicity, manifestation can be described as emanation.
items.inference: Because each state is internally manifold, it is fitting to understand their shining forth in the form of emanation.
uncertainties: The verse points forward to a later determination (nirṇeṣyate) without specifying where.
items.plain_english: But the waking state and the others each have many divisions, which will be determined later; therefore it is fitting that their shining forth takes the form of emanation.

rows.grounds: adverb of consequence; sandhi form of ataḥ

items.question: How does the Lord move from indifference to engagement with manifested entities?
premises: The Lord pervades entities by his own awareness.
Those entities become the means of his activity.
Through them he causes the abandonment of his own state of indifference.
items.inference: By pervading entities with his own awareness, the Lord uses them to relinquish his indifference and engage in manifestation.
uncertainties: The agency of etais is compact; it can be read as instrumental means or as the entities prompting the change.
items.plain_english: Therefore, pervading those entities by his own awareness, the Lord causes that state of indifference of his to be abandoned through them.

items.question: What effect does the expansion of the power of knowledge have on entities abiding in that knowledge?
premises: The power of knowledge undergoes expansion.
Some entities abide in the state of that knowledge.
Those entities possess an unfolding radiance of their own.
items.inference: When the power of knowledge expands, entities abiding in that knowledge attain fullness with their own radiance unfolding.
items.plain_english: This is the expansion of the power of knowledge: entities abiding in the state of that knowledge attain fullness, with their own radiance unfolding.

items.question: Why is there supreme contraction at the level of Sadyojāta?
premises: A supreme contraction occurs at the level of Sadyojāta.
At that level beings do not attain firm abiding in their own nature.
Lack of firm abiding in one's own nature constitutes contraction.
items.inference: Because firm abiding in their own nature does not arise there, the level of Sadyojāta is characterized by supreme contraction.
uncertainties: The referent of eṣāṃ is context-dependent and not explicitly identified in this verse.
items.plain_english: At the level of Sadyojāta there would indeed be supreme contraction, because firm abiding in their own nature does not arise for them.
